title: Uniform eventual kernel equality for ideal-power cohomology
statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], I an ideal of A, f: X -> Spec A a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], J=I O_X the extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and F a coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Fix q >= 0. Let M_n=H^q(X,J^n F) as an A-module by restriction along A -> Gamma(X,O_X), with the image products of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] and cohomology of [pqf-def-cohomology]. Suppose i_(k,n): J^k F -> J^n F is any family for n<=k whose composite into F is the inclusion of J^k F. Write mu_(k,n) for the induced A-linear cohomology maps. Then there exists c0 >= 0 such that for every c >= c0 and every n >= c, ker(mu_(n,0))=ker(mu_(n,n-c)).

source.place: Lemma 02OA, proof of (3); independently read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02OA

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-powers-ideal-rees-finite] and monic inclusions into F to obtain finite graded M over B=Rees(I), composition of transitions, and compatibility with scalar-induced homogeneous products. Thus K=sum ker(M_n -> M_0) is a graded B-submodule.

B is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-rees-algebra-noetherian], so K is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. Replace finite generators by their homogeneous components y_j in K_(d_j); let c0 bound their degrees, with zero for an empty generating set.

For c>=c0 and n>=c, comparison of degree-n components expresses every element of K_n as a sum b_j*y_j, b_j in I^(n-d_j). Each term vanishes after transition to n-d_j because y_j maps to zero in M_0; as d_j<=c, composition makes it vanish at n-c too. Conversely a class vanishing at n-c vanishes at 0 by composition. This gives equality of the kernels for every such c.

theorem cohomology_powers_ideal_kernel_bound
    (A : Type v) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {X : Scheme.{v}}
    (I : Ideal A) (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [IsProper f] (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hJ : J = (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
      (I.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv.hom)).comap f)
    (F : X.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F) (q : ℕ)
    (i : ∀ (k n : ℕ), n ≤ k →
      (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι k).2 F ⟶
        Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι n).2 F))
    (hi : ∀ (k n : ℕ) (h : n ≤ k),
      i k n h ≫ Scheme.idealModuleProductι (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι n).2 F =
        Scheme.idealModuleProductι (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι k).2 F) :
    ∃ c0 : ℕ, ∀ c : ℕ, c0 ≤ c →
(∀ n : ℕ, c ≤ n →
          LinearMap.ker ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
              ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).map
            ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace q).map (i n 0 (Nat.zero_le n)))).hom =
          LinearMap.ker ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
              ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).map
            ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace q).map
              (i n (n - c) (Nat.sub_le n c)))).hom)
